papers.title: A Draft Genome Assembly of Argania spinosa Provides Insights into Lipid Metabolism-Associated Genes and Repeat-Rich Genome Architecture.
papers.abstract: Argania spinosa (L.) Skeels is an ecologically and economically important Moroccan tree valued for its oil-rich seeds and adaptation to arid environments. Here, we generated and characterized a genotype-specific draft genome assembly of Z-AL-IV-13 using approximately 82.7 GB of Illumina sequencing data. The final contamination-screened assembly comprised 584.21 Mb across 139,591 sequences, with an N50 of 6.84 kb. BUSCO analysis identified 59.1% complete, 25.4% fragmented, and 15.6% missing conserved eudicot orthologs, while independent k-mer analyses indicated incomplete genome representation
papers.summary: This study presents a draft genome assembly of Argania spinosa, an economically important Moroccan tree known for its oil-rich seeds and arid adaptation, using Illumina sequencing. The assembly is highly fragmented (N50 of 6.84 kb, 59.1% BUSCO completeness) and the authors highlight lipid metabolism-associated genes and a repeat-rich genome architecture. The work provides a first genotype-specific genomic resource for argan but is limited by its draft quality.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology-Guided Identification of Orientin from Passiflora incarnata Reveals Neuroprotective Effects Against Glutamate-Induced Excitotoxicity Through Regulation of Calcium Homeostasis.
papers.abstract: Epilepsy is a chronic neurological disorder in which current antiseizure medications are limited by incomplete seizure control and variable therapeutic responses, highlighting the need to identify new bioactive candidates. Passiflora incarnata (P. incarnata) has demonstrated neuropharmacological and anticonvulsant properties. However, the individual phytochemicals and molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain incompletely characterized. In this study, we integrated network pharmacology with cellular validation to identify epilepsy-relevant phytochemicals of P. incarnata and evaluate
papers.summary: Using network pharmacology combined with cellular experiments, the authors identified orientin from Passiflora incarnata as a candidate neuroprotective compound for epilepsy. Orientin appears to protect neurons from glutamate-induced excitotoxicity by regulating calcium homeostasis. The work provides mechanistic support for the traditional anticonvulsant use of P. incarnata and nominates orientin for further investigation.

papers.title: HIT-MAP: A scalable approach to multimodal mapping of subcellular organization.
papers.abstract: Multimodal mapping of subcellular protein organization through imaging and interaction proteomics has been mostly confined to large consortia, owing to high per-target costs, reliance on target-specific antibodies or libraries of epitope-tagged cDNAs, and the lack of unified pipelines for coordinated data acquisition. Here, we present HIT-MAP (high-throughput integrated tagging for cell mapping), an end-to-end framework that couples endogenous epitope tagging with optimized wide-field immunofluorescence imaging and affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS). Applied to a pilot set of 16 r
papers.summary: HIT-MAP is an end-to-end framework that combines endogenous epitope tagging, optimized wide-field immunofluorescence imaging, and affinity purification-mass spectrometry to map protein subcellular localization and interactions in a coordinated, scalable way. It lowers the cost and technical barriers that previously restricted multimodal subcellular mapping to large consortia, demonstrated in a pilot of 16 targets.

papers.title: An Ontology for Workplace Violence: Protocol to Support Cross-Sector Incident Reporting in Public Services.
papers.abstract: Underreporting is a defining problem in the documentation of workplace violence across public services. This is reinforced by inconsistent, often poor incident descriptions and the absence of a clear, shared nomenclature. Without an ontology-backed structure, similar events are recorded differently across settings or remain uncodable and effectively invisible. Moreover, workplace violence (WPV) is typically registered and studied within sector- and even organization-specific categories and local reporting logics rather than through a shared semantic framework, limiting comparability and cumula
papers.summary: This paper describes a protocol for developing an ontology to standardize how workplace violence incidents are reported across different public service sectors. The goal is to address underreporting and inconsistent documentation by creating a shared semantic framework that allows comparable, cumulative data across organizations. The work is at the protocol stage, outlining the planned approach rather than presenting results.

papers.title: EBV-HSA-RegDB: A database of regulatory interactions between Epstein-Barr virus and human miRNAs.
papers.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a ubiquitous human herpesvirus associated with various malignancies and autoimmune diseases. MiRNAs play crucial roles in viral-host interactions by regulating gene expression post-transcriptionally. Understanding the regulatory networks between EBV-encoded miRNAs and human miRNAs is essential for elucidating viral pathogenesis and identifying therapeutic targets. We reported the EBV-HSA miRNA Regulatory Database (EBV-HSA-RegDB, https://lbcd.ufpa.br/ebvhsa or  https://lbcd.ia.br/ebvhsa ), an integrated bioinformatics resource that combines comparative sequence analy
papers.summary: This paper presents EBV-HSA-RegDB, a curated database of regulatory interactions between Epstein-Barr virus-encoded miRNAs and human miRNAs, built by integrating comparative sequence analysis with other bioinformatics approaches. The resource aims to help researchers map the viral-host miRNA regulatory network underlying EBV pathogenesis and identify potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Unlocking the full potential of spatial omics in plants: practical challenges, solutions, and a path forward.
papers.abstract: Spatial omics technologies provide new opportunities for plant biology by enabling molecular profiling within structurally intact tissues, revealing spatially organized cell states, developmental gradients, and regulatory interactions. While spatial transcriptomics has driven early advances, the field is rapidly expanding toward integrated spatial multi-omics by combining single-cell and spatial transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data. These approaches offer new opportunities to study development, physiology, and plant biotic and abiotic interactions in spatially preserved
papers.summary: This perspective reviews how spatial omics technologies can be applied to plant biology, moving beyond spatial transcriptomics toward integrated multi-omics that combines single-cell and spatial transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data. The authors discuss practical challenges specific to plant tissues and propose solutions and a roadmap for the field. The work is a methodological and strategic guide rather than a primary research finding.

papers.title: MTB-KB: A Curated Knowledgebase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Related Studies.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB), has regained its position as the world's leading killer among infectious diseases. Despite extensive research progress across epidemiology, diagnosis, drug development, treatment regimens, vaccines, drug resistance, virulence factors, and immune mechanisms, MTB-related knowledge remains fragmented across thousands of publications, limiting its application in research and clinical practice. To address this gap, we present MTB-KB, a literature-curated knowledgebase that systematically integrates high-impact findings from eight major
papers.summary: MTB-KB is a literature-curated knowledgebase that systematically integrates high-impact findings on Mycobacterium tuberculosis from eight major research areas, including epidemiology, diagnosis, drug development, treatment, vaccines, drug resistance, virulence factors, and immune mechanisms. It addresses the fragmentation of TB knowledge across thousands of publications by providing a centralized, curated resource. This database aims to support both research and clinical applications in tuberculosis.

papers.title: DHX15 as a novel immune-related prognostic biomarker in breast cancer: An integrated bioinformatics analysis with in vitro functional validation.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is a disease that occurs relatively frequently, and its prognosis and treatment outcomes are not optimal at present. Identifying novel BC biomarkers and therapeutic targets is key. DEAH-box helicase 15 (DHX15) is an RNA helicase that exhibits enhanced activity and is closely associated with tumorigenic potential. Alternative splicing is widely dysregulated in BC. However, the biological function of DHX15 in BC, in addition to its underlying molecular mechanisms, remain unclear. DHX15, a key RNA helicase involved in splicing regulation, was therefore selected to explore wheth
papers.summary: This study identifies the RNA helicase DHX15 as a potential immune-related prognostic biomarker in breast cancer using integrated bioinformatics analysis, and supports the finding with in vitro functional experiments. The authors link DHX15 to alternative splicing regulation and tumorigenic potential, suggesting it may serve as both a prognostic indicator and a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Methods for determining indications for antibiotic prescriptions to facilitate antimicrobial stewardship: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: Effective antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) requires accurate information on the reason for prescribing antimicrobials. To design targeted interventions aimed at improving guideline adherence, accurate information on the indication for each prescription is necessary. This scoping review maps the existing methods used for systematically determining indications for antibiotic prescriptions.
papers.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
papers.summary: This scoping review maps existing methods for systematically determining the clinical indication behind antibiotic prescriptions, a prerequisite for effective antimicrobial stewardship. It catalogs approaches used to capture prescribing rationale, which can inform targeted interventions to improve guideline adherence. The review highlights the need for accurate indication data to design stewardship programs.

papers.title: Multi-omics analysis of extracellular vesicle cargo in cancer.
papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are increasingly recognized as minimally invasive sources of molecular information in cancer, carrying nucleic acids, proteins, lipids, and metabolites that reflect tumor biology. Recent advances in high-throughput sequencing and mass spectrometry have not only enabled multi-omics profiling of EV cargo but also revealed that different molecular layers capture distinct yet complementary aspects of cancer processes. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the rapidly expanding landscape of EV multi-omics, highlighting methodological constraints, the predomin
papers.summary: This review surveys how multi-omics profiling of extracellular vesicle cargo—nucleic acids, proteins, lipids, and metabolites—can provide minimally invasive molecular information about tumor biology. It highlights that different molecular layers capture complementary aspects of cancer processes, while also discussing methodological constraints and current limitations of EV-based multi-omics.

papers.title: ICD-11 and diabetes: opportunities for precision public health through enhanced classification.
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus poses a major global health challenge, yet its intrinsic heterogeneity has been poorly captured by traditional classification systems. The international classification of diseases, tenth revision (ICD-10), built on a phenotype-based framework, lacks the granularity needed to incorporate contemporary molecular insights into diabetes subtypes, hampering both clinical precision and public health surveillance.
papers.summary: This paper argues that ICD-10's phenotype-based diabetes classification is too coarse to capture the disease's molecular and clinical heterogeneity, limiting both precision medicine and public health surveillance. It proposes that ICD-11's expanded classification offers an opportunity to integrate contemporary molecular insights into diabetes subtypes, enabling more precise public health tracking and targeted interventions.

papers.title: IMicAP: an intelligent microbial application platform for knowledge-driven microbiome research.
papers.abstract: Microorganisms play a pivotal role in health and disease, yet microbial research is hindered by fragmented data, heterogeneous knowledge representation, and a lack of integrated analytical tools. Existing databases and knowledge graphs often focus narrowly on genomic information, leaving critical metabolomic and literature-based associations underdeveloped.
papers.summary: IMicAP is presented as an integrated platform for knowledge-driven microbiome research that aims to address fragmented microbial data, heterogeneous knowledge representation, and the lack of unified analytical tools. It seeks to combine genomic, metabolomic, and literature-derived associations into a single intelligent application, though the abstract describes the platform's motivation and scope rather than specific results or validation.

papers.title: Microbiota-derived metabolite signatures in Alzheimer's disease across the cognitive aging continuum: a human-focused systematic review and evidence-weighted knowledge graph.
papers.abstract: Gut microbial metabolism is increasingly implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), preclinical amyloid accumulation, and cognitive aging. However, existing reviews often focus on microbial taxonomy rather than the metabolite mediators that connect the gut ecosystem with AD pathology, neuroinflammation, and cognition.
papers.summary: This systematic review shifts focus from gut microbial taxonomy to the metabolite mediators linking the gut ecosystem with Alzheimer's disease pathology, neuroinflammation, and cognition across the cognitive aging continuum (preclinical amyloid accumulation, MCI, AD). The authors synthesize human evidence on microbiota-derived metabolite signatures and integrate it into an evidence-weighted knowledge graph, providing a structured resource for identifying candidate metabolite biomarkers and mechanistic links.

papers.title: Renal proteomic landscape of a patient with Fanconi renotubular syndrome carrying a novel GATM variant.
papers.abstract: Fanconi renotubular syndrome (FRTS) is a rare Mendelian disorder characterized by proximal tubular dysfunction. FRTS type 1 (FRTS1) has been associated with heterozygous variants in GATM, encoding mitochondrial glycine amidinotransferase. Although GATM-related mitochondrial abnormalities have been proposed to contribute to tubular injury, the molecular alterations in human kidney tissue remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This case report describes a patient with Fanconi renotubular syndrome carrying a novel GATM variant and presents a proteomic analysis of the patient's kidney tissue. The study aims to characterize molecular alterations in the renal proteome associated with GATM-related mitochondrial dysfunction, providing insight into disease mechanisms at the tissue level.

papers.title: CfDNA methylation profiling in blood following moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury using brain cell type-enriched signatures: A pilot study.
papers.abstract: The human brain consists of diverse cell types that collaboratively perform complex functions and form intricate neuronal networks. When traumatic brain injury (TBI) occurs, multiple molecular pathways involving diverse cell types are activated in response to injury. Understanding how brain cell composition is altered during TBI may help improve patient outcomes. Upon brain trauma, neurovascular disruption leads to the release of brain-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA) into peripheral blood. The tissue-specific DNA methylation patterns in this cfDNA have the potential to serve as candidate markers
papers.summary: This pilot study used brain cell type-enriched DNA methylation signatures to profile cell-free DNA in blood from patients with moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury. The authors show that cfDNA methylation patterns can reflect brain-derived DNA release and potentially reveal changes in brain cell composition after injury. The work suggests cfDNA methylation as a candidate biomarker approach for TBI, though validation in larger cohorts is needed.
